title: Comunicado 2026-09-23
summary: The SARB MPC raised the repo rate by 25bp to 7.25% in a unanimous decision, explicitly 'adopting a more restrictive monetary policy, with rates above longer-term levels' to stop the intensifying fuel shock from triggering second-round effects. Versus the July statement, the committee moved from a split 4-2 hold that judged the stance 'appropriate for now' to a unanimous hike: the fuel shock it had hoped was unwinding intensified (Brent assumptions revised up sharply, headline peak near 5.7%), global rates rose with the Fed's first hike in three years, and market-based expectations picked up while survey expectations stay near 4% against the 3% target. The QPM baseline has the rate broadly stable for the rest of the year, so no further hike is pre-signalled, but both risk scenarios (higher global rates, higher expectations and wages) imply one to two more hikes, and the MPC says it 'will act as needed'. Growth concerns rose (Q2 contraction, 2026 growth cut to 1.2%) but did not restrain the tightening; the 'measured approach' wording and rand resilience are the only softening notes.

key_quotes.quote: Against this backdrop, the committee decided to raise the policy rate by 25 basis points, to 7.25%, effective from 25 September. The decision was unanimous.
key_quotes.context: Unanimous 25bp hike, after July's 4-2 hold with two members preferring a hike

key_quotes.quote: To prevent this, we are adopting a more restrictive monetary policy, with rates above longer-term levels.
key_quotes.context: Explicit move to a more restrictive stance to block second-round effects of the supply shock

key_quotes.quote: That said, they remain high, with longer-run expectations around 4% rather than our 3% target.
key_quotes.context: Expectations still above target; market-based measures picking up after the fuel increases

key_quotes.quote: The forecast from our Quarterly Projection Model (QPM) has the policy rate broadly stable through the remainder of this year.
key_quotes.context: Baseline path does not pre-signal another hike; risk scenarios do
